title: Alkynes: Terminal Acidity, Kucherov Hydration, & Polymerization
topics: Alkyne Structure (sp Hybridization, 1σ + 2π bonds, 1.20 Å length, 837 kJ/mol)
Terminal Alkyne Acidity (50% s-character, pKa ≈ 25, Sodium Acetylide with NaNH₂)
Diagnostic Heavy Metal Tests: Tollens' Reagent (White Ag-ppt) and Fehling's/Cu₂Cl₂ (Red Cu-ppt)
Kucherov Hydration (1% HgSO₄ / 40% H₂SO₄, 60°C → Enol → Ketone; Acetylene → Acetaldehyde)
Cyclic Trimerization (3 HC≡CH over Red-Hot Fe at 873 K → Benzene)
Stereospecific Alkyne Reductions: Lindlar's Catalyst (cis-alkene) vs Birch Reduction (trans-alkene)
quickSummary: Terminal alkynes are acidic (sp C has 50% s-character) and form precipitates with Tollens' (white Ag-acetylide) and Cu₂Cl₂ (red Cu-acetylide). Kucherov hydration yields ketones (acetylene yields acetaldehyde). Lindlar gives cis-alkene; Birch gives trans-alkene.
summary: Master alkyne terminal acidity, diagnostic precipitate tests, Kucherov hydration, cyclic polymerization, and stereospecific reductions.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.1 Terminal Alkyne Acidity & Diagnostic Tests
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.1 Terminal Alkyne Acidity & Diagnostic Tests

summaryBox.title: Terminal Acidity
summaryBox.takeaway: sp-Carbon (50% s-character) makes C-H acidic. Tollens' gives white Ag-ppt; Ammoniacal Cu₂Cl₂ gives red Cu-ppt. Internal alkynes DO NOT react.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
TERMINAL ALKYNE DIAGNOSTIC TESTS

1. Tollens' Test:
   R-C≡C-H + [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ → R-C≡C-Ag ↓ (White Precipitate) + NH₄⁺ + NH₃

2. Ammoniacal Cuprous Chloride Test:
   R-C≡C-H + Cu₂Cl₂ + 2 NH₄OH → R-C≡C-Cu ↓ (Red Precipitate) + 2 NH₄Cl + 2 H₂O

Internal alkynes (R-C≡C-R') do NOT have acidic terminal protons and give NO precipitate!
conceptBreakdown.content: Because $sp$-hybridized carbon atoms have $50\%$ $s$-character, their valence electrons are tightly held by the nucleus, conferring high electronegativity and making the terminal $\text{C-H}$ bond acidic ($\text{p}K_a \approx 25$). Reaction with heavy metal cations produces insoluble metal acetylide precipitates.

conceptBreakdown.title: 6.2 Kucherov Hydration & Stereospecific Reductions
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
KUCHEROV HYDRATION & REDUCTIONS

• Kucherov Hydration:
  R-C≡C-H + H₂O ──[1% HgSO₄ / 40% H₂SO₄, 60°C]──► [R-C(OH)=CH₂] ──[Tautomerism]──► R-CO-CH₃ (Ketone)
  (Exception: HC≡CH yields Acetaldehyde CH₃CHO)

• Stereospecific Reductions:
  ├── Lindlar's Catalyst (Pd/CaCO₃/quinoline) + H₂ ──► cis-alkene (Syn-addition)
  └── Birch Reduction (Na / Li in liquid NH₃)      ──► trans-alkene (Anti-addition)

• Cyclic Polymerization:
  3 HC≡CH ──[Red-hot Fe tube, 873 K]──► Benzene (C₆H₆)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Kucherov Hydration**: Mercuric sulfate-catalyzed hydration adds water across the triple bond to form an enol, which tautomerizes to a ketone (Ethyne exclusively yields acetaldehyde).
• **Lindlar's Reduction**: $\text{Pd/CaCO}_3$ poisoned with quinoline/lead acetate reduces alkynes with syn-stereospecificity to *cis*-alkenes.
• **Birch Reduction**: Sodium or Lithium in liquid ammonia reduces alkynes with anti-stereospecificity to *trans*-alkenes.

quickRevision: Terminal alkynes give white ppt with Tollens' and red ppt with Cu₂Cl₂.
Kucherov hydration of propyne gives acetone.
Lindlar's catalyst produces cis-alkenes; Birch reduction produces trans-alkenes.
